prompt: Implement a genetic-algorithm fitness function: count the character positions where a candidate string matches the target. Complete the score method in the starter file.
explanation: Evolutionary algorithms need a fitness function that scores how close each candidate is to the goal; for string evolution the simplest score is the count of matching positions. Math.min of the two lengths keeps charAt inside bounds when the strings differ in length. Comparing chars with == is fine here because charAt returns a primitive char.
hints: Decide the loop bound before you start: only a position that exists in BOTH strings can match, so the smaller of the two lengths is how far you may go.
Compare candidate.charAt(i) == target.charAt(i) inside the loop and count the matches.
